This is a lesson on one conga part the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)**. It is one of the first patterns to learn, so this page starts from it and takes it into the band. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Conga parts](index.qmd#congas)

## The pattern

Only the two right-hand open tones of the tumbao, on 4 and the and of 4. The first thing to play.

It belongs in *Son montuno*, *Cha-cha* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the cha-cha style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Step 1: Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1), slowly

**How to play it.** Only the two right-hand open tones on 4 and the and of 4. Strike near the edge with the fingers flat and let the drum ring.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="congas bass" data-staves="congas" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)","opts":{"congas":"opens"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's congas off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="congas bass" data-choice-label="Conga part:" data-choices='[{"label":"Open tones only (learning the tumbao, 1)","opts":{"congas":"opens"}}]'></div>

## In other styles
